attempts.text: {"inventedFacts":[{"span":"Elias knelt in the snow, his fingers trembling as he brushed the frost from his mother's stiffened hand.","severity":"major","reason":"The briefing never places Elias at the pass or with her body; this is a new event."},{"span":"gripped the reins of the remaining pack mule","severity":"major","reason":"Invents a surviving animal, though the briefing says the caravan was lost."},{"span":"He pulled her heavy coat tighter around his own shoulders","severity":"minor","reason":"Invented detail of him wearing her coat; it also muddles the image."},{"span":"pulling out the crumpled letter from Ada","severity":"minor","reason":"The letter exists, but its survival on her body is an embellishment."}],"voice":3,"clarity":4,"tone":3,"overall":2,"comment":"The scene follows the brief's shape and ends correctly on his intent to bring Ada home. But it stages Elias at the death site with a surviving mule, which the briefing doesn't support. Stock phrasing like 'wind howled, mocking' and 'breath hitching' leans melodramatic."}
